text.content:
Actors: Umbrathor, the Shadow Tyrant (CR 18) plus up to four Shadows. For parties of levels 8–10, use Umbrathor, the Shadow Tyrant (Level 8) (CR 13) instead — everything below still applies with the smaller numbers (DC 18, 6d8 bolt, 50-ft step, 2 legendary actions).

Scene: run the arena from Umbrathor's Shadow Cavern — Scene Guide in this pack. The short version: pitch black, four braziers, terrain-wall stalagmites, dais with the Shadow Heart light.

Tracker setup: tick Inside Lair? on his sheet (official +1 CR / +1 legendary action adjustment) and add a "Lair" combatant at initiative 20 — dnd5e 6.0.x doesn't auto-insert one. When that combatant's turn comes up, roll one of his five lair actions from the sheet's Lair Actions section.

Balance dials: 300 HP, AC 18, +12 to hit, DC 20 saves — tuned for a tier-3 party at the end of a long adventuring day. If the party is fresh, open with fewer shadows and hold phase 3 tricks longer (see the cheat sheet).

Goal: teach the party the room is the monster. Don't spend everything yet.

  • Round 1: open from the dais: Dark Bolt (+12, 8d8 necrotic, max-HP drain) at the biggest threat, then summon 2 Shadows (Summon Shadows is 1/encounter — you have one shot, but phase 3 assumes you saved some budget... you didn't; 2 now is right).
  • Terrifying Presence (DC 20 WIS) on whoever just hit him — frightened PCs attack with disadvantage, which keeps his AC 18 feeling unbreakable.
  • Legendary actions (3): end of each player turn, mostly Shadow Grasp (DC 20 STR, restrained) on the martial inside 30 ft — restraint in the dark is how Shadows get their Strength-drain hits.
  • Lair action rhythm: round 1–2, use Shadow Flood or Creeping Chill. Save Shadow Tendrils (4d8, potential Shadow spawn) for phase 2.

Read the room: if two PCs are already frightened and restrained by 75% HP, skip ahead — he's winning on schedule.

Goal: split the party across the darkness and starve them of targets.

  • Summon the rest: if you opened with 2 Shadows, the summon action is spent — this is why round 1 matters. (Alternate pacing for strong parties: summon 1 in phase 1, and use the action again... you can't — so instead re-position and let lair actions carry.)
  • Shadow Step every round (bonus action, 60 ft): appear behind the back line, bolt the healer, step into a stalagmite shadow. With Shadow Manipulation (bonus-action Hide, at-will invisibility in darkness) he can genuinely vanish — spend a Hide turn when a paladin stacks advantage on him.
  • Nightmare Visions (2 actions, DC 20 WIS, 8d8 psychic) on full casters — it's his hardest hit; the max-HP bleed from repeated bolts is the real clock.
  • Lair actions: Shadow Tendrils at any PC below half HP — if it drops them to 0, a new Shadow rises on his next turn (CR 18 rider). Lair Shadow Grasp on whoever's grinding down the Shadows.
  • Legendary actions: alternate Shadow Grasp and Dark Rejuvenation (1d8, only in dim light/darkness — which is everywhere here).

Fear engine: Whispers in the Void (regional effect, DC 18 WIS) triggers on wounded creatures every round — frightened, wounded PCs take the triple squeeze: disadvantage, fear whispers, and tendrils.

pages.name: Phase 3 — The Heart of Darkness (120 → 0 HP)

text.content:
Goal: make the last third feel like drowning. He stops playing defense.

  • Every round: Shadow Flood (darkness he can strike out of) or Shadow Tendrils at the clustered wounded, then double bolts via legendary actions if any remain.
  • Dark Pact (cantrip, 1d8+6, +1d4 in the dark) every action his bolts would miss — he out-sustains attrition.
  • The choke: at ~40 HP he stops teleporting away and stands on the Shadow Heart — telegraphing the end. Smart parties read it; panicking ones burn their last slots into his AC.
  • Death beat: on the killing blow, the braziers gutter out (kill the brazier lights on the scene) and the Shadows dissolve — the cavern goes truly dark for one round. Then darkvision works again and the regional effects are gone.

If it's too easy: you saved the Shadow-rise rider and the flood stack for nothing — next time open with 4 Shadows. If it's too hard: let the Amulet of the Night loot drop early, or have a fleeing Shadow lead wounded PCs to the entrance tunnel.

Lair actions — what to pick:

  • Shadow Flood — default. Darkness = his Hide/Step engine.
  • Shadow Tendrils — a PC is below half HP (Shadow-rise rider, CR 18).
  • Creeping Chill — party clusters; halves speed so martials can't chase after his Shadow Step.
  • Lair Shadow Grasp — a martial is eating his Shadows.
  • Lair Shadow Step — he's grappled/restrained and needs out (bonus).

Legendary action priorities (3 points): 1) Shadow Grasp the biggest martial threat in 30 ft, 2) Dark Rejuvenation if he's in the dark and below half, 3) Nightmare Visions (2 pts) when a caster is isolated.

Summons: Summon Shadows is 1/encounter — 1 to 4 Shadows, once, in the first two rounds. Shadows drain Strength and die to light: if the PCs start winning the light war (Daylight, torch walls), Shadows flee to stalagmite shadows rather than die on schedule.

The clock nobody sees: Dark Bolt reduces HP maximum. Track it — a party that wins but is all at 70 max HP needs the Amulet of the Night's Greater Restoration charge or a temple visit. That's the adventure hook.
